edges.description: MED12 variants cause the neurodevelopmental phenotype, although the intervening neural developmental mechanisms are unresolved.

MED12-depleted HEK293 cells receive siRNA-resistant wild-type, p.Arg1148His or p.Ser1165Pro MED12. Target-gene qPCR, protein expression and co-immunoprecipitation distinguish defective repression from loss of protein stability, Mediator incorporation or G9a binding.
edges.limitations: An engineered non-neuronal cell assay supports a specific biochemical defect. It does not demonstrate recruitment failure at REST sites, neuronal differentiation defects or the complete clinical phenotype.

edges.description: Lymphoblastoid cells carrying p.Arg1148His or p.Ser1165Pro show increased FOS and reduced EGR1 after serum induction.
edges.limitations: These are non-neuronal patient cell lines. The extensive p.Arg1295His fibroblast promoter studies in the same paper cannot be assumed to apply to the Ohdo alleles.
edges.target: Altered Serum-Responsive FOS and EGR1 Expression

nodes.description: After serum stimulation, p.Arg1148His and p.Ser1165Pro patient lymphoblastoid cells show increased FOS and reduced EGR1 expression. The extensive JUN-promoter, MMP3 and REST2 analyses in the same paper mainly concern p.Arg1295His fibroblasts and cannot be assigned wholesale to MKB syndrome. These experiments support variant- and cell-context-dependent transcriptional responses, not a demonstrated neuronal developmental cascade.
nodes.id: Altered Serum-Responsive FOS and EGR1 Expression

evidence.snippet: The two mutations related to Ohdo syndrome (R1148H and S1165P) also lead to an up regu- lation of FOS and a down-regulation of EGR1 (Supplementary Material, Fig. S7), illustrating the regulatory role of MED12 in IEGs expression regulation.

evidence.snippet: FLAG-tagged MED12 mutants p.Arg1148His and p.Ser1165Pro were unable to repress CHRM4, SNAP25, and SYN1 expression.

nodes.description: In HEK293 cells depleted of endogenous MED12, wild-type MED12 suppresses derepression of CHRM4, SNAP25 and SYN1, whereas p.Arg1148His and p.Ser1165Pro are impaired in this rescue. Comparable protein abundance, Mediator incorporation and G9a binding argue against simple protein instability or loss of the G9a interface. Impaired recruitment to RE1-bound REST was proposed by analogy with other MED12 alleles; it was not directly measured for these Ohdo variants in the original experiment.

nodes.description: Intellectual disability is a defining feature; severity and adaptive function vary among affected individuals.

evidence.snippet: XLOS is characterized by intellectual disability, blepharophimosis, and facial coarsening.

evidence.reference_title: Mutations in MED12 cause X-linked Ohdo syndrome.
evidence.snippet: The occurrence of three different hemizygous missense mutations in three unrelated families affected by Ohdo syndrome MKB type shows that mutations in MED12 are the underlying cause of this X-linked form of Ohdo syndrome.

evidence.reference_title: MED12 Mutation in Two Families with X-Linked Ohdo Syndrome.
evidence.snippet: Segregation analysis revealed a hemizygous variant in the affected boys and a carrier status in the unaffected mothers. Also, the mutation was confirmed in the maternal affected uncle.

This detected a novel de novo hemizygous MED12 missense variant NM_005120.2:c.4831C>T p.(Arg1611Cys), classified in line with American College of Medical Genetics and Association for Clinical Genomic Science 2019 guidelines as likely pathogenic and absent from the population database, gnomAd.

nodes.description: Pathogenic MED12 variants alter transcriptional regulation by Mediator. MED12 is part of the MED12-MED13-cyclin C-CDK8 regulatory module, but membership in that module does not establish a uniform CDK8 catalytic defect in MKB syndrome. Experiments with p.Arg1148His and p.Ser1165Pro retain MED12 expression, Mediator incorporation and G9a binding while revealing selective transcriptional abnormalities.
